**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/25 (Thu) 23:50  
[FACT] The user works on mathematical or logical problems.  
[USER_SAID] The user experiences difficulty finding solutions to problems during the day.  
[USER_SAID] The user often finds solutions while falling asleep or waking up.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The phenomenon described by the user is called the incubation period.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The incubation period refers to the process of unconsciously working on a problem in the mind.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] During the incubation period, the brain continues to process information and make connections.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The breakthrough experienced by the user when waking up or falling asleep is a normal part of the problem-solving process.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The process of "sleeping on it" is a common way to find solutions.  
[USER_SAID] The user most often finds solutions before falling asleep.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] There may not be a significant difference between finding a solution before falling asleep or upon waking up.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Both instances are part of the incubation period.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Letting the mind relax and wander can lead to new connections and solutions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Whether it's before falling asleep or upon waking up, the brain has had time to incubate and process information.
